title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 66 (Computer Related Offences)

content.overview: Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides that if any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine, or with both. Section 66 converts the civil wrongs listed in s. 43 into criminal offences when done with the specified mens rea.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is a s. 43 act proved? (2) Was it done dishonestly or fraudulently? (3) Civil s. 43 still available in parallel?
content.study:
Always prove a concrete s. 43 act first, then dishonestly or fraudulently. Do not treat s. 66 as a free-standing vague cyber offence.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Link to s. 43
sections.body: The actus reus is any act referred to in section 43 (unauthorised access, data theft, virus introduction, damage, disruption, etc.).

sections.heading: Mens rea
sections.body: Dishonestly or fraudulently — the element that converts civil s. 43 liability into criminal s. 66 liability.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both — as enacted.

sections.heading: Parallel civil path
sections.body: s. 43 compensation remains available for the same acts without the criminal mens rea threshold.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Map facts to a s. 43 clause; prove dishonestly/fraudulently; state punishment; note civil alternative.

examples.title: Fraudulent data download
examples.body: Person dishonestly downloads confidential data without permission — s. 43 act + dishonestly → s. 66 offence; civil s. 43 also open.

hypotheticals.question: Is every s. 43 act automatically a s. 66 crime?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 66 requires the additional element of dishonestly or fraudulently.

distinctions.title: s. 66 criminal vs s. 43 civil
distinctions.left: Punishment when s. 43 acts are done dishonestly or fraudulently.
distinctions.right: Compensation for s. 43 acts without criminal mens rea.

misconceptions.correction: s. 66 only criminalises s. 43 acts done dishonestly or fraudulently.
